reviews.text: The service is terrible. Going there for advice is a waste of time.

I was very dissatisfied with the doctor's treatment.

I was bleeding after the injection, but the doctor finished without checking.

Although I've been a patient here until now, I'm going to change hospitals.

My dog ​​had what appeared to be a tooth fall out, so I had it checked during a checkup, but they said it wasn't chipped. Later, while playing with him at home, I noticed the chipped tooth. If I had taken him to another hospital, they would have had no choice but to extract it. They said that if I had noticed it sooner, they might have been able to find a way to avoid extraction.

My dog ​​is a calm dog who likes people. He doesn't bite, so I'm sure the vet would have been able to check the tooth.

I paid a lot of money for an examination, so why didn't they notice the chipped tooth?

If you want a thorough examination, I definitely recommend not going here.

My dog ​​🐶 had to have an important tooth extracted. It was general anesthesia, which was very stressful. I'm so sorry, but I don't want to give it even a 1 star rating.

I don't even want to give it one star.
First of all, I suppose the high price is unavoidable because it's Pets First pricing.
However, the staff's knowledge is lacking, and they can't answer all my specific questions. Furthermore, the veterinary nurse has long nails.
I've never seen anyone in a profession that deals with animals have such long nails. Don't they consider the possibility of injuring the animals when they touch them?
There's absolutely no sense of trust or confidence in them.
I've owned pets for many years and visited many hospitals, but this is the first time I've seen such a sloppy hospital with inadequately trained staff.
I will never go there again.
Everyone is always so kind and helpful. Thank you!

I came here for a checkup. 
There was no wait time and the process was smooth! They are also kind to pets, so I feel safe leaving my pet there!

It's a bit of a walk from the station, but they have a partnership with the pet shop next door, so you can see the waiting time through the glass, and the time flies by! Consultations are also quick and easy!

Every time I go, everyone is friendly. It's a bit more expensive than other places. No major illnesses yet. I only went there for my puppy's vaccinations. I don't know about anything else, but it's great!
All the doctors and nurses are very kind.

This hospital actually has doctors who deserve zero stars or even negative ratings.

I used it for vaccinations for a dog I adopted from the pet shop next door.

It's open every day except New Year's Day.

It's conveniently located and clean. The receptionists and nurses are kind. It's always crowded, so reservations are recommended.

The prices are high. Surprisingly expensive!

* Nail trimming
* Paw pad hair trimming
* Anal gland expression
* Ear cleaning (ear hair trimming not included)
All of these cost 1000 yen, making it feel like money has wings (the going rate for these services is usually around 500 yen).

During vaccination, they'll perform a "stool test" using the feces sample attached to the thermometer unless you refuse (this also costs 1000 yen).

The vet told me, "We found some kind of bacteria in the stool sample," fueling my anxiety and leading me to further tests and medication (it was a bacteria that could be treated with Biofermin, and when I asked about the dosage, she seemed unaware, which was appalling).

Furthermore, the female vet who diagnosed my dog ​​with "loose knee joints" kept asking me about the timing of the neutering surgery at every vaccination appointment. Just to be sure, I had a doctor at another hospital examine my dog, who advised, "There's no need to be overly concerned. Just manage his weight and make sure he gets plenty of exercise to strengthen his leg muscles." The female vet gave absolutely no such advice. Also, a breeder who has been raising the same breed as my dog ​​for many years says, "Neutering stops growth, so small dogs with weak knees almost always experience joint dislocations. It's better to wait until they are fully grown, around 1.5 to 2 years old, before surgery." Articles about the effects of spaying and neutering on the musculoskeletal system in dogs are readily available online.

This hospital only cares about making money, not the health of dogs.
